subject: sentences
title: Short vowel sentences
about: Fourteen short sentences built only from short-vowel words and the CKLA Unit 1 tricky words, so every word is readable in September. Reading whole sentences smoothly is the bridge from sounding out words to understanding.
tip: Have him read it once slowly, then again like he is talking, and ask what the picture has to do with it.

cards.text: The cat sat on the mat.
cards.note: tricky word the: the e says /u/
tricky word a: it says /u/. In has, the s says /z/

cards.text: The dog can run and jump.
cards.note: tricky word the: the e says /u/. Blend nd in and, mp in jump

cards.text: I have a big red bus.
cards.note: tricky words I: says its name, always a capital; have: the e makes no sound

cards.text: The hen is in the pen.
cards.note: tricky words the: the e says /u/; is: the s says /z/
tricky word the: the e says /u/. In box, x says /ks/

cards.text: The fish swims in the pond.
cards.note: tricky word the: the e says /u/. In fish, sh is one sound; in swims, the last s says /z/
tricky words the: the e says /u/; is: the s says /z/

cards.text: Max has a box of chicks.
cards.note: tricky word of: o says /u/, f says /v/. In chicks, ch is one sound and ck makes one /k/
tricky word the: the e says /u/. In hill, ll makes one /l/
no tricky word. In Beth, th is one sound; in socks, ck makes one /k/
tricky word who: wh says /h/, o says /oo/. A question: let his voice go up

cards.text: The frog can hop on a log.
cards.note: tricky words the: the e says /u/; a: it says /u/. Blend fr in frog
tricky word what: wh says /w/, a says /u/. A question: let his voice go up
